CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is West Manggarai Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Manggarai Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Manggarai.
4. Woman is a person who has reproductive organs that can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding. 5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
7. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness or causes death.
8. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
9. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
10. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a decent living care and maintenance.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id

12. Services for women and children are actions that must be immediately taken including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against victims.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Community, the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Court, social institutions or other parties who know or hear of the impending or completed occurrence of violence against women.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
16. Women and Children Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P3A is an institution providing services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
19. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.

www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id

20. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE.

Article 1

Services also include protection for women and children victims of violence.

Article 2 Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims.

Paragraph (3) - Gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women;

www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id - Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings; so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Paragraph (4) Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and class.

Paragraph (5) The best interests of the victim are all actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, Society, Legislative Bodies, Judicial Bodies, then the best interests of the victim must be a primary consideration.

Article 3

The Objectives of Services and Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence are to provide services and protection for women and children victims of violence that are gender-based and in the best interests of children occurring in the household and or public sphere.

Article 6

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance, whether medical, psychological or legal, and to receive guarantees of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be pursued continuously, sustainably, in a directed manner and guarantee the growth and development of children physically, mentally, spiritually and socially so as to realize a good life and to become potential, resilient successors of the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also guarantees that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on 10 December 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id the Government, and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as Mothers of the nation and children as the next generation of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 7

1. The Regent establishes a public service work unit that functions as a facilitator for P3A.
2. P3A as referred to in paragraph (1) in handling services and protection for women and children victims of violence may establish partnerships with social community institutions and customary functionaries engaged in the field of services and protection for women and children.
3. Further provisions regarding P3A institutions shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VI

ASSISTANCE

Article 11

Assistance is carried out by persons or bodies/institutions that have expertise in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence and have cooperated with P3A.

Article 4

What is meant by "receiving protection" is obtaining protection from individuals, groups or institutions, both Government and Non-Government.

Obtaining information about the existence of complaint centers, Women and Children Service Centers (P3A) and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to assistance and development of case handling.

www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id - What is meant by "Integrated Services" is services that include medical, medicolegal, psychosocial and legal.

What is meant by "Continuous Handling" is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of their good name.

CHAPTER VII

FUNDING

Article 12

1. Funds for the provision of services and protection for women and children victims of violence are sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD) of the Regency.
2. funds as referred to in paragraph (1) may also come from other lawful sources.

CONCERNING

Article 3

What is meant by "gender-based violence" is an act based on gender relations that places women in a subordinate position to men.

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be pursued continuously, sustainably, in a directed manner and guarantee the growth and development of children physically, mentally, spiritually and socially so as to realize a good life and to become potential, resilient successors of the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also guarantees that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on 10 December 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id the Government, and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as Mothers of the nation and children as the next generation of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is West Manggarai Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of West Manggarai Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Manggarai.
4. Woman is a person who has reproductive organs that can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding. 5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
7. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness or causes death.
8. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
9. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
10. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a decent living care and maintenance.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id

12. Services for women and children are actions that must be immediately taken including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against victims.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Community, the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Court, social institutions or other parties who know or hear of the impending or completed occurrence of violence against women.
14. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
16. Women and Children Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P3A is an institution providing services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
17. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
19. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.

www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id

20. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE.

Article 1

Services also include protection for women and children victims of violence.

Article 2 Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims.

Paragraph (3) - Gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women;

www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id - Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings; so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Paragraph (4) Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and class.

Paragraph (5) The best interests of the victim are all actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, Society, Legislative Bodies, Judicial Bodies, then the best interests of the victim must be a primary consideration.

CHAPTER IV

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 5

Every victim has the right to receive protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions whether Government or Non-Government.

www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id

Article 4

What is meant by "receiving protection" is obtaining protection from individuals, groups or institutions, both Government and Non-Government.

Obtaining information about the existence of complaint centers, Women and Children Service Centers (P3A) and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to assistance and development of case handling.

www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id - What is meant by "Integrated Services" is services that include medical, medicolegal, psychosocial and legal.

What is meant by "Continuous Handling" is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of their good name.

Article 7

1. The Regent establishes a public service work unit that functions as a facilitator for P3A.
2. P3A as referred to in paragraph (1) in handling services and protection for women and children victims of violence may establish partnerships with social community institutions and customary functionaries engaged in the field of services and protection for women and children.
3. Further provisions regarding P3A institutions shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 10

P3A managers are obliged to organize services and protection in accordance with the service principles as referred to in article 9.

Article 9

Services and Protection for victims are carried out free of charge, quickly, safely, with empathy, non-discriminatory, easily accessible and with guaranteed confidentiality.

I. GENERAL

Services and protection for women and children constitute a series of activities that must be pursued continuously, sustainably, in a directed manner and guarantee the growth and development of children physically, mentally, spiritually and socially so as to realize a good life and to become potential, resilient successors of the nation with noble character and a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also guarantees that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on 10 December 1948 and ratified CEDAW (Convention on The Elimination of All Forms Of Discrimination Against Women) with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, and is therefore obliged to comply with these provisions.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id the Government, and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as Mothers of the nation and children as the next generation of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially www.jdih.manggaraibaratkab.go.id the Government, and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all the formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination. Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women of 1999 it is stated that women as Mothers of the nation and children as the next generation of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.
